transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you; could you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Nice to meet you, Doctor. Well... I suppose I'm here because I keep forgetting things. Things I really shouldn't. 

Like... missing my heart follow-up appointments, or forgetting to call the clinic back. Even just... going to do a repair job and realizing I didn't bring the right tools with me. It's just... yeah, that's mostly it.
Have you experienced these memory and organizational problems throughout your entire life, or is this something that has started more recently?

I suppose... it's been my whole life. Not just recently. 

Even back when I was a boy in grade school... I was always that kid. The one who couldn't stay in his seat. I'd, uh... I'd blurt out answers a lot. Always getting notes sent home to my parents for talking too much. 

So... yeah. It goes way back.
Looking at your life today as an adult, do you still find yourself feeling physically restless or having trouble sitting still for long periods of time?

Well... yes, I suppose so. 

Since I've had to... slow down a bit. With my walks and the projects I used to do around the house. When I try to just sit still, it's... it feels like there's a motor running inside me. Just humming away. And I don't really have a good place to put that energy anymore. So... yeah. It's still there.
When you are working on a task or project, how often do you find that you have trouble keeping your attention on it until it is finished?

I suppose... it happens a fair bit. 

Even when I'm just trying to sit at the bridge table. Or... we have these Fix-It Friends planning meetings. I mean to pay close attention when I sit down. But... after a little while, my mind just sort of slides off. I'll realize I missed half of what was said. 

So... yes. It happens.

When you look back at your life, would you say your primary struggle has been more with staying focused on tasks, or has it been more about your physical restlessness and tendency to act or speak without thinking?

I don't really know... I haven't ever tried to weigh them against each other. 

It's all just... part of how I've always been, I suppose. I couldn't really tell you which one is the main issue. They just both happen.
In your daily life as an adult, how often do you find yourself interrupting others while they are speaking?

Well... I suppose I do that sometimes. 

If I'm at the center... and I hear some folks talking about a project, or maybe going over a hand of cards... I'll just sort of jump in. I give my opinion before anyone actually asks for it. 

I usually realize after the fact that I just barged right in. But... yes. It happens.
Looking back over the last six months, would you say you have been experiencing these issues with restlessness and interrupting others just as frequently as you did when you were younger?

I couldn't really say... it's hard to compare now to fifty years ago. 

I don't really keep track of it like that. I suppose it's just... always been this way. I haven't really noticed any big change one way or the other lately.

When you are in a situation where you are expected to remain seated for a long time, such as in a movie theater or at a long meeting, how difficult is it for you to keep yourself from getting up or moving around?

Well... I suppose it's a bit hard. I don't really go to movies much anymore. 

But if there's a meeting... or even just when I'm having lunch with the guys... I don't usually stay in my chair the whole time. I'm always popping up to... I don't know, refill my coffee, or go look at the notice board. 

I just end up moving around to check on things while everyone else stays seated. That's just how I am.

When you think about the various challenges we've discussed—like forgetting things, trouble focusing, feeling restless, and interrupting others—would you say you have had at least six specific examples of these types of behaviors occurring frequently in your life?
I don't know about counting them up like that... six examples, I mean. I suppose we've talked about a few things today. But putting a number on it... I really couldn't say for sure.

Besides the problems with forgetting appointments and losing focus during meetings, do you often find yourself losing important items like your keys, glasses, or tools, or perhaps making careless mistakes in tasks because you didn't pay close attention to the details?

Not really... no. I usually know where my keys and things are. And... well, since I'm not working anymore, I'm not really doing any complicated tasks to be making mistakes on. Just... regular things around the house. So, no, I wouldn't say I do that.

When you think about the times you've struggled with these issues, would you say that you have experienced these difficulties with restlessness and acting without thinking just as often as you have experienced the trouble with focus and forgetting things?

Well... I suppose the moving around and the... acting fast, that happens more often. The other stuff, the focus and the forgetting... I don't really notice that as much. It's mainly just the not being able to sit still.
Have these struggles with restlessness and speaking without thinking ever caused significant trouble for you in your life, such as problems with friends, family, or your past employment?

Well... I suppose it's caused some issues. Down at the senior center, I help out with the repair group... or I used to, mostly. They just... they can't really count on me the way they used to, I guess. And... well, the doctor's office has been calling. Chasing me down about missing my heart follow-ups. So... yes, it causes some trouble.

Are these difficulties with restlessness and interrupting others something that happens mostly just at the senior center, or do you find yourself doing these same things when you are at home or out in other social situations?

I'm not... I haven't really kept track of it. I suppose it's just... wherever I happen to be. I don't go out all that much besides the center anyway, mostly just home. So... I don't know. Probably both, I guess.
